external_evidence.claim: Muted autoplay is always allowed; autoplay with sound needs a prior user interaction with the domain or a high Media Engagement Index; play() without permission rejects with NotAllowedError

Since iOS 10, <video autoplay> and video.play() without a gesture are allowed when the source has no audio track OR the element is muted; autoplaying videos start only when visible and pause when scrolled out; playsinline is required or iPhone forces fullscreen; play() returns a Promise that rejects when conditions fail

NN/g eyetracking: users scrutinise photos of real people and ignore stock/decorative imagery; on a team page the user spent 10% more time on portraits than on bios that took 316% more space; 'on personal websites, users want to see the person behind the site'

Cerf, Frady & Koch 2009 (J. Vision 9(12)): faces attracted gaze 16.6× more than expected from size/position, text 11.1×, independent of task; Djamasbi et al. 2010 (IJHCS): Generation Y users fixated a face within their first two fixations on homepages
external_evidence.source: https://jov.arvojournals.org/article.aspx?articleid=2122098 (direct fetch returned HTTP 403 this session), https://users.wpi.edu/~djamasbi/PDFS/2010%20djamasbi%20et%20al-%20IJHCS%20(journal%20version).pdf — both reached only through a Perplexity citation

The recommendation therefore keeps the loop small, silent, grayscale and slower than the type — the face is a credibility signal, not the message

external_evidence.claim: Moving content that starts automatically, lasts more than 5 s and is presented alongside other content needs a user mechanism to pause, stop or hide it — a 5.875 s loop that repeats indefinitely meets all three conditions, so a keyboard-operable pause control is required on any autoplaying placement

React does not serialise the boolean `muted` prop into server-rendered HTML (long-standing facebook/react issue #10389), so a <video muted> in JSX can reach WebKit un-muted at parse time; set video.muted = true imperatively before play() and/or use defaultMuted

placements.name: Right column beside role · statement · ledger (recommended)
placements.where: .inner becomes a two-column grid at ≥720px: `grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) var(--portrait-w)`; eyebrow, h1, actions, availability span both columns (grid-column 1 / -1); the portrait <figure> sits in column 2, grid-row 3 / 6 (role → ledgerRow), align-self start. .ledgerRow stays in column 1 and uses its existing ≤1100px single-column form (grading note under the ledger) at every width, since the portrait now owns the right side. Below 720px the figure becomes an 88px square stamp absolutely positioned top-right of .inner on the eyebrow row.
placements.why: The name keeps its full 7.5rem measure (a 2-column split at h1 height would wrap 'Vikram Deshpande' at 1440 where it runs ≈900px wide); the face sits at the reader's eye line next to the sentence that is the pitch; the 4:5 box is defined by CSS width + aspect-ratio so it reserves space at first paint (CLS 0); with width capped so height ≤ the role+statement+ledger rows at 1280x720, TC-HERO-08/09 hold by construction.
placements.risks: At 1280x720 the poster (≈205×256 CSS px ≈ 52k px²) out-sizes the h1 (≈490×67 ≈ 33k px²) and becomes the LCP element — acceptable because it is a 41 kB AVIF in static HTML with fetchpriority=high; assert LCP tag ∈ {IMG, H1}. The 640x360 source cropped 4:5 is 288×360 px, so at 230 CSS px on a 2× screen it is upscaled ≈1.6× (soft, not broken); the still poster is sharp. VIS-01 baseline changes.

placements.name: Full-bleed grayscale backdrop behind the type (replacing/over the atmosphere)
placements.where: <video> absolutely positioned in .stage, object-fit cover, dimmed to ~35% with a top-to-bottom ink gradient, grayscale; type unchanged on top.
placements.why: Cinematic, and full-viewport elements are excluded from LCP by heuristic so it cannot become the LCP element.
placements.risks: 640×360 stretched to 1920 is a 3× upscale — visibly soft on every desktop; a face behind type fights the type (contrast over eyes/glasses); it violates 'the scene is never the content' and would need dimming so heavy the face stops reading as a person; on phones a cover-cropped 16:9 shows a shoulder, not a face, unless a second portrait cut is produced; keeps the GPU busy alongside the GLSL atmosphere (two layers) — the hero explicitly caps DPR for mobile frame rate. Not recommended with this source file.

placements.name: Stamp: small rounded square (112–128px) at the eyebrow row's right, all breakpoints
placements.where: position absolute top-right of .inner, aligned with the eyebrow baseline; no grid change; poster only below 720px, loop above.
placements.why: Zero layout risk, one CSS rule set, identical on every device, never LCP (smaller than the h1 everywhere), the 1:1 crop is 360×360 source so it is sharp at 128 CSS px @2×.
placements.risks: Too small to carry the credibility signal NN/g documents — at 112px on a 1440 screen it reads as an avatar chip, not a portrait; the face is 40px tall. Highest total score only because it risks nothing; it also achieves little. Choose it only if P1's VIS-01 rebaseline or grid change is judged out of scope for this cycle.

recommendation.one_line: A silent, grayscale 4:5 portrait of the same face that speaks in the MiniVic panel, standing in the hero's empty right half beside the sentence that is the pitch — poster first, loop later, never moving for a reader who asked it not to.

poster.file: public/assets/my_avatar.avif (41 343 B, 1480×826) via , WebP 66 470 B second, PNG 178 777 B last; the is the LCP candidate and stays at opacity 1 from first paint — it must NOT take the heroRise opacity entrance (LCP excludes opacity-0 elements and the old HeroAvatar comment records the same rule)
poster.eager_weight: 41 kB image; the 160 kB mp4 is never eager (preload="none", no src attribute in HTML) — eager assets total ≤ 500 kB with ≥ 450 kB headroom
poster.no_video_poster_attribute: <video poster> takes a single URL and cannot use AVIF/WebP negotiation, so the poster is the <picture> layered UNDER the video, not the attribute

video_attributes.markup: muted loop playsInline preload="none" aria-hidden="true" tabIndex={-1} disablePictureInPicture disableRemotePlayback; NO autoplay attribute (play is programmatic after the gate so the file never joins the load path); NO src/<source> in server HTML; NO controls
video_attributes.imperative: before play(): video.muted = true; video.defaultMuted = true (React may not serialise `muted` — Assumed); video.play().catch(() => keep poster)
video_attributes.gate_sequence: 1) matchMedia('(min-width: 720px)').matches && !matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches && !(navigator.connection?.saveData) — else stop, poster only; 2) wait for window load (or readyState === 'complete') then requestIdleCallback (setTimeout 1200 ms fallback); 3) IntersectionObserver on the figure, threshold 0.25: entering → set src=/assets/my-hero-avatar.mp4, load(), play() on canplay; leaving → pause(); 4) document visibilitychange hidden → pause; 5) matchMedia change listeners for reduced-motion and width → pause + remove src if the condition turns false
video_attributes.why_this_order: Chrome: muted autoplay always allowed (Verified). WebKit: play() without gesture allowed when muted, and it will refuse when not visible — the observer only calls play() when in view (Verified). The load-event + idle gate keeps the decode off the LCP path, which is what the old HeroAvatar learned the hard way (its comment: the observer fired 'immediately after hydration' and put the download on the load path).

crossfade.rule: Poster never animates. Video sits above the poster at opacity 0 and transitions to 1 over 600 ms var(--motion-ease-standard) only when ALL of: 'playing' fired, !video.paused, video.currentTime > 0.04, video.videoWidth > 0 (the old component's guard, kept verbatim — it stops the 'dark empty panel' bug it documents). On pause / error / stalled / visibilitychange hidden / out of view → opacity back to 0 over 300 ms so the still shows through. Both layers share `filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.04)` on .portraitMedia (one composited filter, not two), object-fit cover, identical object-position, so the still and the first video frame are the same crop of the same shoot and the fade is a change of breath, not of picture.
crossfade.loop_seam: 5.875 s loop: the first and last frames are not identical (talking head), so a hard cut is visible every 6 s. Cheap mitigation without touching the asset: on 'timeupdate' when currentTime > duration − 0.25 begin a 250 ms fade to 0.55 opacity and back to 1 on 'seeked'/'playing' — the poster is underneath so the seam is a soft blink. Better fix later (cost gate, ask first): re-render the loop as a palindrome or a 10–12 s idle at 720p.

monochrome.rule: .portraitMedia { filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.04); } on the wrapper around <picture> and <video>. Mandatory: the source frames are warm sunset colour, and on this site gold means 'this figure has a source' (CLAUDE.md prime directive 4). MONO-04 would not catch it (it reads computed CSS colours, not pixels), so a new assertion must (TC-HERO-18 below). No gold border, no gold ring, no gold caption — the portrait is not a sourced claim. Border: 1px var(--card-border); background: var(--ink-800) while the poster loads; border-radius: 4px (the ledger uses rules, not cards — keep the radius small so it reads as a print, not a chip).

keyboard_and_a11y.pause_control: <button type=button aria-pressed=false aria-label="Pause the portrait"> at the figure's bottom-right, 40×40 hit area (min 24×24 per WCAG 2.5.8; 48 preferred by this site's actions), glyph ‖ / ▶ drawn in CSS or inline SVG in --white; focus-visible: outline 2px solid var(--white); outline-offset 3px (matches .primaryAction:focus-visible). Toggling sets a `paused` state that the gate respects (a user pause wins over the IntersectionObserver re-entry). Rendered only when the video is eligible (≥720px, motion allowed) so nothing focusable exists for a reader who has no motion to stop. Tab order: it comes after the statement and before the ledger, matching DOM order.
keyboard_and_a11y.img_alt: "Portrait of Vikram Deshpande" — truthful and short; do not name the city (the backdrop is not verifiably Melbourne)
keyboard_and_a11y.video: aria-hidden=true, tabIndex=-1 — it is a decorative re-rendering of the image the already describes
keyboard_and_a11y.reduced_motion: poster only; the video never receives a src, the button is not rendered, and TC-CINE-06/07 stay satisfied because the poster is not part of the heroRise/heroFade set

relation_to_minivic.same_face: Both loops and the still are the same shoot; the hero loop (640×360, silent, 5.9 s) is the quiet presence, the panel loop (1280×720, 12.3 s) is the one that speaks. The hero never plays audio and never carries a 'LIVE' label — the old HeroAvatar's 'SUBJECT · LIVE' tag is exactly the boast the tone linter exists to fail.
relation_to_minivic.wiring: lib/avatarContext.tsx already exposes useAvatarSpeaking() (Verified). Rule: while the MiniVic panel is open (or speaking === true) the hero loop pauses and fades to the poster — one face does not talk in two places, and a phone should not run two decoders. Resume on panel close via the normal gate. The caption 'Silent loop · he speaks in the panel' (figcaption, mono caption style .grading) is the only copy; it is literally true and points the reader to the synthetic introduction, which the Listen section already labels as synthetic.
relation_to_minivic.do_not: Do not reuse my-avatar.mp4 (1.1 MB) in the hero — it would be the largest eager-adjacent asset on the page for a 12 s idle that the panel already owns.

playwright_guards.assert: `#hero [data-testid=hero-portrait] img` is visible, naturalWidth > 0, alt === 'Portrait of Vikram Deshpande', currentSrc ends with .avif in Chromium; computed opacity ≥ 0.99 within 200 ms of #hero visible (the poster never fades in)

`#hero video` has attributes muted, loop, playsinline, preload=none, aria-hidden=true, no autoplay, no controls; at DOMContentLoaded its src is empty; after `load` + 2500 ms it has src ending my-hero-avatar.mp4, paused === false, currentTime > 0.04, and computed opacity > 0.9 (Chromium muted autoplay is always allowed — if CI's software renderer still refuses, launch with --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required for this spec only)

with page.emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'}): no request whose URL contains my-hero-avatar.mp4 is made within 4 s (page.on('request')), the video has no src, the pause button has count 0, the poster img is visible at opacity ≥ 0.99

with page.route('**/my-hero-avatar.mp4', r => r.abort()): the poster stays visible, video computed opacity ≤ 0.05, no uncaught page error (page.on('pageerror'))

Tab from the statement reaches `#hero button[aria-pressed]`; Enter toggles aria-pressed to true, video.paused === true, aria-label becomes 'Play the portrait'; Space toggles back; focus-visible outline colour is achromatic (white)

sum of transferSize for image resources under /assets/ loaded before the load event ≤ 500 000 B, and the mp4's requestStart is after loadEventEnd (performance.getEntriesByType('resource'))
PERF-07 extension: the final LCP entry's tag is 'IMG' or 'H1' (never 'VIDEO' or 'CANVAS') and startTime ≤ 2500 at 1280x720
at viewport 390×844 the figure's box is ≤ 96×96 and its top ≤ the eyebrow's bottom; `#hero video` count 0 after 3 s (no video below 720px)
TC-HERO-01…11 unchanged; TC-HERO-03 must still read the statement at `#hero p` nth(2); TC-HERO-04 still counts exactly 3 li; VIS-01 rebaselined once and the PNG inspected before commit

recommendation.effort: ≈ 1 focused cycle: Hero.tsx (+ ~90 lines: figure, gate hook, toggle), Hero.module.css (+ ~110 lines incl. 3 media queries), 10 new hero.spec.ts tests, VIS-01 rebaseline, screenshots at 390/834/1280/1440(/1920). Delete components/site/HeroAvatar.tsx in the same commit (dead, references vanished classes) or the dead-code posture of the repo is weaker than before the change.
open_limits: Source resolution: 640×360 cropped 4:5 is 288×360; at 230 CSS px on 2× it is upscaled ≈1.6×. A 720p re-render of the same loop (cost gate — ask) would remove the softness; the spec does not depend on it.
The loop's seam every 5.875 s is visible; the fade mitigation above hides it, a palindrome re-render fixes it.

No verified award-listed monochrome portfolio with a filmed self-portrait was found within the search budget; the placement rests on the eye-tracking evidence and this site's own constraints, not on precedent.
